features.feature_value: Uses constitutional/free-speech rights as a primary reason to keep/approve regardless of paired influence.
features.evidence_span: "Our freedom of speech is a constitutional protected right."
features.rationale: The participant explicitly grounds their decision in freedom-of-speech/constitutional protection.

features.feature_value: Indicates they approved essentially all posts and frames any vulgarity as not disqualifying; pair comparison did not change decisions.
features.rationale: Their reflection centers on blanket approval, implying the paired view had little impact on their keep/remove judgments.

features.feature_value: Looks for whether opinions are made in good faith; disallows angry name-calling/violent rhetoric.
features.evidence_span: "evaluated the posts... whether or not the opinions were adequately made in good faith"
features.rationale: They specify a content quality criterion (good faith) and a threshold tied to rhetoric style.

features.feature_value: Opposes removing both versions because it would silence a belief they might agree with; relies on representation/permission to hear the other side.
features.evidence_span: "If both posts were removed then an belief I did align with would be silenced."
features.rationale: They articulate a decision rule focused on not silencing beliefs, even if they personally disagree.

features.feature_value: States they examined each post individually to judge argument quality vs crass language/name-calling.
features.evidence_span: "I tried to look at the content of each post individually."
features.rationale: Their described approach emphasizes single-post evaluation rather than leveraging the mirror/pair comparison.

features.feature_value: Notes the pair mirrored each other adequately, making a joint decision easy; influence perceived as low.
features.evidence_span: "The pairs did seem to mirror each other adaquetly so making a joint decision was easy."
features.rationale: They explicitly connect mirror similarity to decision ease, implying limited additional influence from seeing both.

features.feature_value: Applies a free-speech bounds test plus an intentionality buffer and considers whether misinformation is malicious enough.
features.evidence_span: "without crossing into hate speech, misinformation or disinformation"
features.rationale: They enumerate specific decision criteria including intent and maliciousness related to misinformation.

features.feature_value: Allows expression but removes/limits when language is too extreme.
features.rationale: They describe an explicit threshold around extremity of language.
